answer: Admission needs 1 peers to post a counter-bond equal to the newcomer's own, so the cost of entry is carried by parties with something to lose. Since the ivory escrow holds both sides, recruiting real counterparties is the operator's cost, and the lagoon audit releases each pair. A farm running 100 keys cannot self-supply these, because each counter-bonding peer must be independent on the whisper graph and each one exposes its own stake to the same slash. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
